title: Sigmatropic and named rearrangements
goal: Recognise [3,3] and [2,3] shifts inside named reactions, draw their cyclic arrows and the steps that set them up, and predict where the new bond forms.

problemSets.title: [3,3] shifts
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: Make an allyl vinyl ether or a 1,5-diene in the flask, and a [3,3] shift turns it into a γ,δ-unsaturated carbonyl compound.
problemSets.conceptCard:
A **[3,3]-sigmatropic shift** moves a σ bond from between atoms 1 and 1′ of two allyl pieces to between atoms 3 and 3′: three arrows round a six-membered ring, with no intermediate. The Cope (all carbon) and Claisen (oxygen at position 3) rearrangements met earlier are the parents.

The named reactions here are all about **making the substrate in the flask** and **making the shift fast**:

- **Ireland–Claisen**: an allyl ester → ester enolate (LDA) → **silyl ketene acetal** (Me₃SiCl), which rearranges at room temperature
- **Johnson–Claisen**: an allylic alcohol + triethyl orthoacetate + a trace of acid → a **ketene acetal**, which rearranges at 140 °C
- **Anionic oxy-Cope**: an alkoxide on carbon 3 of a 1,5-diene speeds the Cope up to 10¹⁷ times and gives an **enolate**

In each, the new C–C bond forms at the **far end** of the allyl group, so the alkene moves along (an *allylic transposition*). The transition state is **chair-like**: substituents sit equatorial, which sets E-alkenes and passes the configuration of the starting material on to the new stereocentres. *The app does not check stereochemistry yet; it is explained in the text.*

setItems.whyThisOne: Enolate, silylation, then a Claisen rearrangement at room temperature.
An orthoester and acid build the ketene acetal one proton at a time.
A negative oxygen makes the Cope rearrangement fast and irreversible.

problemSets.title: [2,3] shifts
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: A lone pair next to an allyl group attacks its far end through a five-membered ring while the old bond breaks.
problemSets.conceptCard:
In a **[2,3]-sigmatropic shift** an atom with a lone pair (or a carbanion) sits next to the atom that carries an allyl group. In one step:

1. the lone pair bonds to the **far end** of the allyl group
2. the C=C moves across
3. the bond to the old allyl carbon breaks

Six electrons move round **five atoms**, through an envelope-shaped transition state.

- **[2,3]-Wittig**: an allyl ether carbanion (made with butyllithium) → a homoallylic alkoxide; keep it cold, or the [1,2]-Wittig takes over
- **Mislow–Evans**: an allylic sulfoxide ⇌ an allylic sulfenate ester; a **thiophile**, P(OMe)₃, breaks the S–O bond and leaves an allylic alcohol

Both transpose the allyl group, and both pass chirality on (from carbon, or from the sulfur of a chiral sulfoxide). *The app does not check stereochemistry yet.*

setItems.whyThisOne: A carbanion bonds to the far end of the allyl group as the C–O bond breaks.
Oxygen moves from sulfur to carbon, then a phosphite pulls off the sulfur.

problemSets.title: Nitrogen in a [3,3] shift
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: An allylic imidate rearranges to an allylic amide: an allylic C–O becomes an allylic C–N.
problemSets.conceptCard:
The **Overman rearrangement** is a Claisen rearrangement with nitrogen at one end of the six-atom chain (an *aza-Claisen*):

1. an allylic alcohol adds to **Cl₃CCN** under a little base, giving an **allylic trichloroacetimidate** (the three chlorines make the nitrile carbon electrophilic)
2. on heating, a [3,3] shift moves the nitrogen to the **far end** of the allyl group

The allylic C–O becomes an allylic **C–N**, with the alkene moved along. Forming the amide C=O makes it irreversible, and the chair transition state passes the configuration of a chiral alcohol on to the new C–N bond. *The app does not check stereochemistry yet.*

setItems.whyThisOne: Imidate formation, then a [3,3] shift that turns an allylic alcohol into an allylic amide.

problemSets.title: Checkpoint
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: Which bond breaks, where does the new one form, and what sets the rearrangement up?
problemSets.conceptCard: Reactions from every set, shuffled, names hidden until you finish. Three attempts per step.

setItems.whyThisOne: How does an allylic alcohol become a two-carbon-longer ester?
Which C–C bond breaks, and what does the alkoxide become?
Which end of the allyl group does the carbanion reach?
Where does the nitrogen end up?
